title: Hideout Web
intro: A mobile web menu for an international bar in Busan that opens from a QR code at the table. Designed around how the bar actually runs, for the people ordering and the people pouring.
brief: On any given night, Hideout's guests come from all over the globe. The goal wasn't just to put the menu on a phone, but to improve ordering for both sides of the bar: easier for guests to browse, clearer for staff to take orders from, and simple to update without a designer every time a cocktail changes.
did: I designed the full experience, from structure and interaction to visual style, and shot the drink photography myself. Guests can discover drinks in a swipeable carousel or use a compact list when they already know what they want, and switch the whole menu between English, Korean and Spanish.
Guests build their order on their own phone, and the waiter view always shows it in English, so staff can read it at a glance on a busy night.
The menu, specials and events live in simple data files apart from the design, so the bar can change prices or announce an event without touching the layout.
